newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sharp says air conditioner sales to decline.
newsitem.headline: Sharp says air conditioner sales to decline.

text.p: Sharp Corp said on Tuesday that it expects industry-wide domestic sales of air conditioners to decline to just over 7.5 million units in the year from October 1996 to September 1997, compared with 8.0 million units for the current year.
"Sales in the upcoming year are unlikely to be as good as the current year during which we saw exceptionally robust sales in June and July thanks to hot weather," a Sharp spokeswoman said.

But she also said there were several positive factors for the upcoming year, such as increasing demand for air conditioning units during the winter season and an expected increase in the number of housing starts before the consumption tax hike slated for April.
In the year from October 1994 to September 1995, all Japanese makers of air conditioning units, including Toshiba Corp and Hitachi Ltd, sold 7.7 million units.
